I remember reading about it back when it first came out IIRC the problem was that the last 0,5 GB of VRAM was much slower to access, essentially making performance worse once a game used 3,5 GB.

That's right, and the cause of this was something that's extremely common throughout the industry. nVidia does it, AMD does it, and Intel does it. The actual performance degradation from the segmented memory was only seen in extremely demanding setups (ie.demanding games on ultra settings and > 1080p resolutions.) If that situation changed your view of nVidia then that's what happened, but it's really not that big of a deal. The only reason it became a major controversy to begin with was because people were going by the memory reporting of hardware monitoring overlays that showed they only had 3.5GB of total physical VRAM. This led them to the conclusion that they had been physically shortchanged and deceived. Upon closer examination, that was not the case. The last .5GB doesn't perform as well as the first 3.5GB but that doesn't mean it isn't there and it also isn't indicative of shady business practices.

The internet likes to over-react at the first sign of a scandal. There's a reason that particular controversy died down about as quickly as it started.
